title: Cobalt Retail - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Onboarding kickoff for Cobalt Retail. Covered integration options (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC), security/compliance requirements, initial pilot scope (search & recommendations), success metrics, and next steps for pilot onboarding and benchmark run. Action items assigned for share of docs, infra checklist, and kickoff of staging deployment.
topics: integration options: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC
security: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
pilot scope: product search and recommendations
action_items: Alex Martinez: Send onboarding playbook, deployment checklist and estimated pricing sheet - due 2027-02-03
Priya Singh: Schedule technical workshop for model selection and quantization recommendations - due 2027-02-01
Jordan Lee: Provision staging tenant and invite Cobalt team to console with RBAC - due 2027-01-31
Samir Kahn: Share sample traffic profile and query latency SLOs - due 2027-01-29
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 summary + security questionnaire answers
Schedule infra deep-dive with SREs (Priya + Leo + Samir)
Provision staging environment and start smoke test with 50k requests/day profile

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-27
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM); Dana, Samir, Maya, Leo (Cobalt)

00:00 Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm alex from redwood, i'm the AE on this account, super excited to kick this off. how are you all?
00:06 Dana: good thanks, hi alex. Samir and maya here as well. we wanted to cover security and the pilot scope today.
00:12 Alex: perfect. quick agenda, we'll run through onboarding timeline, integration paths (hosted, dedicated, private), security checklist, then pilot scope for search and recommendations and next steps.
00:25 Priya: hi! i'm priya, i'll be your se. i'll focus on the technical bits — model choices, latency/cost tradeoffs and staging requirements.
00:33 Samir: hi, quick note, our main constraint is sub-100ms 95th pct for search responses under typical load, cost target is under $0.002 per query if possible — rough numbers.
00:45 Priya: okay noted, that's tight for production but doable with batching and caching; for search we usually recommend smaller encoder models for embeddings and a reranker for relevance. quantization helps on dedicated infra.
00:58 Maya: security is our primary blocker for production — SOC 2, encryption at rest and in transit, audit logs, and we need SSO via SAML. also KMS for key management.
01:10 Jordan: we have a standard pack of docs; we'll share our SOC 2 overview and a security questionnaire. redwood supports SAML SSO, KMS integrations, and audit logs in the console. for private deployments we can do VPC peering or dedicated private control plane.
01:25 Dana: when would dedicated vs hosted make sense? we don't want to commit to dedicated unless it's necessary.
01:30 Priya: hosted is fastest to get started; predictable latency and lower operational burden. dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and better tail latency guarantees; private VPC/on-prem is for strict data residency and regulated workloads. we can start hosted for the pilot and move to dedicated once throughput needs justify it.
01:45 Leo: how does routing/fallback work if capacity is constrained?
01:48 Priya: we have smart routing -- requests can be routed by policy (latency, cost, region). if capacity is constrained we can fallback to compatible model variants — with transparent metrics in the console.
02:05 Samir: can we do KV cache/prefix caching for search? that would help reduce latency on repeat queries.
02:10 Priya: yes we support KV cache and prefix caching, and batching policies. we'll recommend cache TTL and how to set batch sizes based on your qps distribution.
02:25 Dana: useful. on the pilot, our goal is to validate relevance lift and measure latency/cost. success criteria: 10% uplift in click-throughs, 95th pct latency under 120ms, and cost under our target.
02:40 Alex: perfect, that's a clear set of success metrics. pilot scope recommended: index-based embeddings pipeline + a reranker on Redwood hosted; we'll run embedded benchmark and a small production-like replay.
02:55 Maya: regarding logs, can we get audit logs exported to our SIEM?
03:00 Jordan: yes, audit logs can be exported to S3 or pushed to your SIEM via webhook; we also support long-term retention as an add-on.
03:15 Dana: timeline — how quickly can we get staging up?
03:20 Jordan: we can provision a staging tenant within 2 business days once legal/TOS signed and we have SSO/KMS config; staging will have console access and RBAC so you can invite users.
03:35 Samir: for benchmarks we'll need a sample traffic profile — we'll share a one-week sample of queries and qps distribution.
03:42 Alex: great. Priya will run the technical workshop to walk model selection and quantization options. we'll propose a pilot plan: 4 week pilot, week 1: staging + smoke tests, week 2: run bench and tune, week 3: relevance evals, week 4: handoff and results.
04:00 Dana: sounds good. one more question — how do you handle sensitive PII during evaluation?
04:05 Priya: you can either hash or pseudonymize in the test set; for private deployments we support customer-managed keys and on-prem options if you need air-gapped processing.
04:20 Maya: what's the expected cost delta if we go dedicated right away vs hosted?
04:25 Alex: dedicated has a monthly commit; up front it's more expensive but unit cost per token is lower for high-volume workloads. for pilot hosted is cheaper and faster. we'll include a cost projection in the pricing sheet.
04:40 Samir: we might want a small bench comparing hosted latency vs a dedicated config with quantized model.
04:45 Priya: yep we'll run the bench — we typically compare identical model variants, quantization levels, and measure 50/95/99 percentiles.
05:00 Dana: ok let's recap actions.
05:05 Alex: recap — Alex sends onboarding playbook, pricing, and SOC2 summary; Priya schedules technical deep-dive; Jordan provisions staging and invites Cobalt users; Samir shares traffic profile.
05:20 Maya: i'll follow up with our legal on the questionnaire.
05:25 Alex: great. any other questions?
05:30 Dana: not at the moment, thanks everyone.
05:32 Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule invites.

End of transcript.
